repo_notes.content: Everything under clients/ is generated by openapi-generator from the YAML files in specs/ and is overwritten on the next spec change, which happens several times a week. Do not document clients/ as if it were authored code and do not dedicate pages to individual generated files or models. A bug in a client is a bug in specs/*.yaml (the upstream contract), in generation.yaml (generator settings and per-language options), or in scripts/generate-clients.sh (the pipeline). Describe those three instead.

Hand-written, and therefore worth reading closely: specs/** (downloaded, not authored here), scripts/**, tests/**, skills/**, .claude-plugin/**, generation.yaml, README.md, docs/i18n/README.*.md, AGENTS.md, website/docs/index.md and website/docs/getting-started.md. Generated, and therefore only worth describing as output: clients/**, website/docs/reference/**, website/docs/SUMMARY.md, website/docs/releases.md, website/docs/llms.txt, website/docs/llms-full.txt, CHANGELOG.md, data/releases.json, .github/images/release-cadence-*.svg, and the region of each docs/*/README.md between the *_METHODS_LIST_START and *_METHODS_LIST_END markers.

Do not describe how Wildberries API tokens are supplied, stored or rotated. The SDK does not manage the token source: it passes through whatever the caller provides. Statements such as 'tokens are read from environment variables' or 'tokens are stored securely' would be claims about the user's setup, not about this code.

The five clients expose the same set of operations, but method names are produced by openapi-generator and differ per language: get_v1_account_balance in Python and Rust, getV1AccountBalance in Node.js and PHP, GetV1AccountBalance in Go. Parameter names differ too — the spec says isAnswered, the Python client takes is_answered — and the request body is named after its model, e.g. put_v3_stocks_warehouse_id_request. Any example must use the spelling of the language it is written in; a name carried over from the spec will not run.

Hosts are declared per path item in the specs, production first and sandbox second, so a single module can span several Wildberries hosts. The Node.js, PHP and Rust clients default their base path to http://localhost and will not reach Wildberries until the host is set explicitly; the Go client resolves it from OperationServers and the Python client from the per-operation _hosts list. This is the single most common reason a correct-looking call fails.

specs/ contains two separate DBS modules — 05-dbs.yaml and 05-orders-dbs.yaml — and four delivery schemes that are easy to confuse: FBS (shipped from the seller's warehouse), FBW (supplied into a Wildberries warehouse), DBS (delivered by the seller) and DBW (delivered by Wildberries from the seller's warehouse). Keep them distinct; conflating them sends readers to the wrong module.
The documentation site at https://eslazarev.github.io/wildberries-sdk/ is written in Russian; the README exists in six languages. The wiki itself should be in English.

pages.title: Overview
pages.purpose: What this repository is: five SDK clients (Python, Node.js, Go, PHP, Rust) for the Wildberries marketplace seller API, each generated from the official OpenAPI specs and republished within a day of any upstream change. Give the reader the shape of the repository — specs in, clients and docs out — and say which directories are authored and which are machine output.

pages.title: Specs as the Source of Truth
pages.purpose: Explain why specs/ is the only place a contract is defined, how the fifteen numbered YAML files divide the API, and what a reader should do when a client looks wrong: fix the spec or patch generation.yaml, never the generated client. Cover the structure the generator depends on — path-item level servers, components/parameters referenced by $ref, request and response models.

pages.title: Spec Modules
pages.parent: Specs as the Source of Truth
pages.purpose: Map each of the fifteen modules to what it covers, roughly how many operations it holds and which Wildberries hosts it talks to: general, items, orders_fbs, orders_dbw, dbs, orders_dbs, in_store_pickup, orders_fbw, promotion, communications, rates, analytics, reports, finances, wbd. Spell out the FBS/FBW/DBS/DBW distinction so a reader can pick the right module on the first try.

pages.title: Authentication, Hosts and Sandboxes
pages.parent: Specs as the Source of Truth
pages.purpose: How a call is addressed and authorised: the Authorization header, the token categories the Wildberries portal issues per API area, hosts declared per operation with a sandbox counterpart, and which clients require the base path to be set by hand because their generated default is http://localhost. Do not describe where the caller keeps the token.

pages.title: Generation Pipeline
pages.purpose: How specs become five published clients: scripts/generate-clients.sh running openapi-generator from a pinned Docker image, the per-language options and template overrides in generation.yaml, the purge step that removes models the upstream spec no longer defines, and why a locally installed generator of a different version must not be used. Explain what cannot be run locally and why.

pages.title: Spec Updates
pages.purpose: The nightly .github/workflows/update-specs.yml job: downloading specs through the S3 mirror because Wildberries' anti-bot protection blocks direct and headless fetching, summarising the diff into a CHANGELOG.md entry, and opening a pull request only when something actually changed.

pages.title: Release and Publishing
pages.purpose: The .github/workflows/generate-clients.yml chain that runs on every push to main: regenerate, bump the version, refresh the README method lists, commit, tag, and publish to PyPI, npm, Packagist and crates.io, with Go consumed straight from tagged subdirectories. Cover the per-language packaging scripts and the github.actor guard that keeps the bot's own commits from retriggering the workflows.

pages.title: Language Clients
pages.purpose: What the five clients have in common — one operation set, native typing in each language, docstrings carried over from the specs, client-side validation of required fields, a shared transport layer — and how to choose between them. Point the reader at the per-language page for installation and the first working call.

pages.title: Python Client
pages.purpose: Installing wildberries-sdk from PyPI, importing a module, constructing Configuration/ApiClient/DefaultApi, calling an operation with the client's own snake_case parameter names, and how pydantic validation and the per-operation _hosts list behave. Show the shape of a real call.

pages.title: Node.js Client
pages.purpose: Installing wildberries-sdk from npm, constructing Configuration with an explicit basePath because the generated runtime defaults to http://localhost, passing parameters as a single request object with the camelCase body key, and awaiting the typed result.

pages.title: Go Client
pages.purpose: Importing one module per API area from clients/go, building NewConfiguration and NewAPIClient, how OperationServers and the API field names on the client work, chaining the request-body builder before Execute, and how authentication is attached.

pages.title: PHP Client
pages.purpose: Installing eslazarev/wildberries-sdk through Composer, obtaining the default Configuration, calling setApiKey and setHost because the generated default is http://localhost, and invoking an operation on the namespaced API class with a Guzzle client.

pages.title: Rust Client
pages.purpose: Depending on the per-module crates from crates.io, building a Configuration, overriding base_path because Configuration::new leaves it at http://localhost, supplying the ApiKey, and awaiting the generated async function in the matching apis module.

pages.title: Documentation Site
pages.purpose: How the Russian-language MkDocs Material site is produced: scripts/build-docs-site.py and the scripts/docsgen package rendering a reference page per operation with examples in all five languages, literate-nav SUMMARY.md, the release-cadence chart generated per language and theme, and the strict build and GitHub Pages deployment in deploy-docs.yml. Note that generated pages are gitignored and rebuilt in CI.

pages.title: Machine-Readable Surface for AI Agents
pages.purpose: What this repository publishes for coding agents rather than people: llms.txt and the llms-full.txt operation digest served from the docs site, AGENTS.md at the repository root, context7.json, the Claude Code plugin declared in .claude-plugin/ and the skill under skills/wildberries-sdk/ with its operation-search script and eval cases. Explain what each one answers and which is the right entry point for a given agent.

pages.title: Tests and Quality Gates
pages.purpose: Why the test suite spells out no operation count and no generated method name, deriving both from specs/ and the clients at run time so that tests do not rot at the next spec update, and what the end-to-end strict documentation build covers. Also cover the security workflows: CodeQL, OpenSSF Scorecard, TruffleHog secret scanning and the per-language dependency audits.
